category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough names the loop-as-list / 'Repeat 1' misconception ('the child uses Repeat 1 over and over instead of Repeat N') with concrete recovery, but no named CS-ed research grounds it and recovery_moves do not branch on what the diagnostic told you about the child.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite CS-ed research in expanded_walkthrough.rationale (e.g., Sorva 2013 on novice loop misconceptions, or Pea & Kurland 1984 on iteration). Branch recovery_moves: if child can articulate why they wrote Repeat 1, drill count semantics with body-loops; if not, drop back to choral 'count the same step' before reintroducing Repeat N notation.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Looper anchors minds_on and consolidation, but consolidation is generically 'Looper's Brag' with discussion_prompts and no quotable refrain children chant back. exit_routine ('write ONE loop on a sticky note') has no memorable chant or sentence frame carried between lessons; no Looper signature line on par with Sounder Sam's example.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Looper a recurring call-and-response refrain children chant back, e.g., Looper: 'Pick the BIG number!' / Children: 'Loops make it SHORT!' Add this chant to consolidation.exit_routine and quote it inside teacher_script in minds_on so it is set up Day 2 and reusable across Lessons 3-5.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression is explicit (long code -> loop count = compression) and the loop-as-list misconception is named precisely, but children do not invent or compare strategies (Station A is 'rewrite using loop cards' per a fixed model) and no named CS-ed research grounds the trap.
category_feedback.required_fix: Add a strategy-comparison move in action.steps: 2-3 pairs share alternative loop solutions for the same shape (e.g., square as 'Repeat 4: forward, turn' vs 'Repeat 2: forward, turn, forward, turn') and discuss which is shorter and why both work. In expanded_walkthrough.rationale name the underlying CS-ed principle (Sorva 2013 notional machine, or Pea & Kurland 1984).

summary: Strong worksheet (Part 2 hexagon transfers Station B stretch; image_assets map to lesson manipulatives) and excellent materials hygiene (puppets explicitly optional, body-loops as no-paper path). Lesson blockers are polish only: add a research citation for the loop-as-list trap, give Looper a child-facing call-and-response refrain, and add a strategy-compare share-out so children see multiple correct loop encodings of the same shape. Worksheet does not need changes.
